bullets.title: Semi tape stabilizing after historic vol; SOX averaged 450bps daily move in June
bullets.body: After a single-session SOX drop of ~8% Tuesday (NDX 3rd largest daily pullback in a year), futures are recovering with semis/AI supply chain bid in pre-market. The selloff was widely attributed to mechanical/technical factors — Korea leveraged ETF unwinding (~$6B sold), quant/passive flows, and Korea tax concerns — rather than any fundamental shift in the AI narrative. SOXX has seen 7 moves of ±5-15% in 30 days; SOX still up ~5% for June.

bullets.title: Micron earnings tonight: buy-side expects $30+ EPS guide, 75% see stock above $1,000 post-print
bullets.body: MU reports FQ3 after close (EPS consensus ~$20.83, revenue ~$35.85B) as the most consensus AI long in the market. Jefferies models FQ4 EPS guide ~$30 vs Street $24.3, GM guide low-80s%, and CY27 EPS ~$200 vs Street $122. Key buyside focus: new Strategic Customer Agreements (60-70% of DDR5 already locked long-term), ASP trajectory, and signals on supply/demand durability. Memory ETF flows strong ($1.2B DRAM, $0.8B MU funds); JPM tactically bullish but flags sell-the-news risk from leveraged ETF crowding.

bullets.title: AI capex cycle accelerating: 5 hyperscalers on track for $730B capex in 2026, up 77% YoY
bullets.body: JPM's mid-year outlook raises SPX year-end target to 7,800 on AI-led capex surge; GOOGL/AMZN/MSFT/META/ORCL collectively account for ~53% of S&P 500 capex (up from ~20% at ChatGPT launch), with total AI-related S&P capex projected at $843B in 2026 and >$1T in 2027. S&P 500 2026/2027 EPS consensus revised up 9%/11% YTD to $350/$390. BofA raised CY30E total semi industry TAM to $2.7T (28% CAGR CY25-30E).

bullets.title: Extreme momentum concentration: 16.9% of S&P stocks explain 80% of YTD returns — lowest since 1990
bullets.body: 22V warns YTD winners are running at 99th percentile 1-month realized vol (97th for 3-month); single-stock vol is at highest ever relative to index vol. Tech/Deep Cyclicals account for ~40% of top decile momentum names. Key trigger: if 2-yr yields break meaningfully above 4.2% toward 4.3-4.5% on hawkish data, severe drawdown in concentrated winners is probable. Recommend hedging via IWM or MTUM put spreads.

bullets.title: Flash PMI robust: US composite 52.2, manufacturing at 4-year high of 55.7 — but employment at cycle low
bullets.body: US Flash PMI rose to 52.2 (May: 51.5) with manufacturing PMI at 55.7, a 4-year high, supporting mid-cycle expansion narrative. However, manufacturing employment fell to 47.0 (cycle low), a divergence worth watching. DM composite PMI also rose 0.8pt to 51.3 globally. JPM expects Fed on hold throughout 2026, then hiking in 2027; core inflation sticky near 3%.

bullets.title: CTA leverage elevated post-June 5 rally; pension funds at 110% funding — mechanical rebalancing risk
bullets.body: CTAs are significantly long but near deleveraging triggers after this week's pullback; VT portfolios de-levered to ~32nd percentile leverage after June 5 selloff (NDX -5%, VIX +6pts). Separately, US pension funds are at 110% funding (highest since 2001), setting the stage for mechanical derisking/rebalancing into equities at the margin. JPM notes gross HF leverage buildup in May was +22% vs 6% avg — historically points to larger-than-average post-expiry declines.

bullets.title: Memory price hike cycle broadening: TSM raising 5-10% on 7nm and below; DRAM spot prices rising
bullets.body: TSM is raising prices 5-10% on 7nm and below nodes due to demand exceeding supply; MediaTek raising chip prices 10-20% citing component shortages. DRAM spot prices rising (mainstream DDR4 +0.28%); commodity DRAM margins surging, causing SK Hynix to ease HBM4 push in favor of commodity DRAM opportunity. Memory chip shortage is only ~50% fulfilling customer demand; prices expected to rise further through 2027. SK Hynix controls 57-61% of HBM market vs 21% for MU and 17-17.6% for Samsung.

bullets.title: SK Hynix filing $29.4B Nasdaq ADR (SKHY) — set to trade July 10, potentially 2nd largest listing ever
bullets.body: SK Hynix plans to raise $29.4B via US ADR listing with 17.79M new shares at ~$145 each in 10:1 ratio; trading begins July 10 on Nasdaq. If successful at top end, would be second largest listing after SpaceX and larger than Saudi Aramco's 2019 IPO. Proceeds fund additional chip capacity, advanced packaging fab, and EUV scanners. Goldman is global coordinator; Citi, BofA, JPM are bookrunners. Listing tests investor appetite ahead of potential Anthropic and OpenAI listings later in 2026.

bullets.title: NVDA chips doubling on China black market; B300 servers ~$1M each amid smuggling crackdown
bullets.body: Nvidia B300 servers have surged to ~CNY7M (~$1M) each since early 2026 as US export crackdowns tighten and Chinese tech companies sustain strong compute demand. RTX 6000 Pro also roughly doubled on grey market. Separately, QCOM is in talks to provide chip-design services to ByteDance based on AlphaWave Semi technology, and ByteDance is in talks for a ~$20B offshore bank loan.

bullets.title: GOOGL replaces VZ in DJIA effective June 29; historical DJIA additions average -3% at T+5
bullets.body: Alphabet joins the Dow Jones Industrial Average replacing Verizon (which represents only 0.5% of DJIA weighting due to low share price), effective June 29 market open. Jefferies notes historical DJIA additions average -3% at T+5 post-inclusion. Honeywell International remains in DJIA under new name Honeywell Technologies after aerospace spinoff.

bullets.title: JPM mid-year derivatives outlook: buy NDX>SPX calls, sell GOOGL/MSFT puts, stay long dividend futures
bullets.body: JPM equity derivatives strategists recommend buying NDX>SPX or XLK>SPX outperformance calls to position for continued AI/tech leadership. Sell GOOGL and MSFT puts as target-buy on the technical pullback while monetizing rich volatility. Stay long 2027 SPX, RTY, and 2026 NDX dividend futures; roll SPX 2026 longs out to 2028. US equity financing at record non-year-end levels on strong leverage demand; vol-of-vol expected to remain elevated even as H2 average vol moderates.

bullets.title: Agentic commerce thesis: AI traffic <1% of e-commerce but growing 8-15x faster, converting 42% better
bullets.body: JPM positions GOOGL, AMZN, and SHOP as primary beneficiaries of agentic commerce. AMZN's Rufus/Alexa for Shopping generated $12B incremental annualized revenue in 2025; SHOP AI-referred shoppers convert 50% higher with 14% higher AOVs; ETSY agentic traffic grew 15x Y/Y. Adobe data shows US AI traffic grew 393% Y/Y in Q1 with 42% better conversion vs non-AI. OpenAI shifted focus from Instant Checkout to app integrations, reducing marketplace cannibalization risk.

bullets.title: Piper Sandler SPX year-end base case 7,500; leadership broadening into SMID-caps and cyclicals
bullets.body: Piper Sandler's 2026 year-end base case is SPX 7,500 with upside to 8,200-8,400 if breadth confirms. Technicals show constructive tape with leadership broadening into SMID-caps and cyclicals; pullbacks appear corrective not trend-changing. Labor force participation ex-retirees at 75.2% and rising, supporting GDP; breakeven payrolls down to 35k/month as population growth slows; unemployment could edge to 3.9% by year-end.

bullets.title: 22V: USD/CNY likely ends 2026 above 6.7; PBOC to ease incrementally amid growth slowdown
bullets.body: 22V warns CNY has appreciated 4% YTD vs their ~2%/year base case, but expects USD/CNY to end above the forward-implied 6.7 level. Chinese domestic growth has weakened significantly since Q2; PBOC likely to pursue incremental easing with PPI deflation risk in early Q3. Fed rate risk, tighter capital outflow regulation, and lack of EU/US coordinated pressure on CNY appreciation all point to limited further CNY strength. A Plaza Accord-type deal deemed unlikely as Beijing views it as a trap.

bullets.title: Online advertising remains healthy at Cannes '26; data infrastructure favored over legacy apps
bullets.body: Citi's Cannes Lions midweek recap notes the online advertising environment is relatively resilient. AI monetization is still early but accelerating; search is transitioning to Answers with query volume growth picking up. Key theme: data infrastructure (Snowflake, Palantir, Databricks) viewed more positively than legacy application software as customers prioritize first-party data control and AI-native workflows over traditional seat-based models.

bullets.title: Regional banks outperforming: KRE +5% over 16 sessions vs SPY -2.8%; curve steepening a tailwind
bullets.body: The belly of the yield curve (2-5yr) has moved above Fed Funds effective rate, positively supporting bank lending dynamics. KRE has outperformed SPY by ~7.8 percentage points over the past 16 sessions. S&P futures +0.33% pre-market; 10-year yield down 4bps to 4.45% as of 8am ET.

bullets.title: Token optimization emerging as dominant enterprise AI theme; not yet a revenue headwind for infra
bullets.body: UBS, Citi, and multiple buy-side checks confirm token optimization is the dominant enterprise AI adoption theme at Cannes and elsewhere — but it is creating demand for cheaper/faster models, not curtailing overall AI infrastructure spending. JFrog checks showed no spend slowdown from optimization pressure; enterprise AI deployment is 'a speed bump not a stop sign.' AWS CEO says 90% of CIOs seeing materially positive ROI on AI vs 0% a year ago.

bullets.title: Oil pulling back: WTI at $72 after Iran de-escalation; diesel below $5, Trump orders DOJ price gouging probe
bullets.body: WTI fell 1.4% to $72.05 as Trump ordered a DOJ investigation into oil company price gouging. US-Iran technical talks resuming next week on Lebanon ceasefire, Strait of Hormuz tolls, and frozen funds. US diesel fell below $5/gallon post-Iran MoU. Lower oil is viewed as a positive for risk sentiment and a disinflationary input. Strait of Hormuz closure stranded ~1,200 cargo ships worth $125B; Qatar expects LNG production within weeks.

bullets.title: Hedgeye rotates to disinflation trade: adds Healthcare (XLV), REITs (XLRE), Housing (XHB)
bullets.body: Hedgeye flagged SOXL's $16B MOC sell order as emblematic of retail leverage in 3x bull ETFs; 7 of SPY's worst 10 names are in leveraged ETFs. USD Index approaching exhaustion above $102. Hedgeye is shifting to a disinflation trade — adding XLV (+1.4% on Tuesday), XLRE (+1.4%), and XHB ahead of expected lower bond yields. S&P 500 immediate-term range cited as 7,266-7,594; UST 10yr range 4.40-4.54%.

bullets.title: BOJ flags inflation risk above 2%, rate hikes needed; PBoC hints at potential cut — diverging CB paths
bullets.body: BOJ Governor Ueda flagged inflation risk above 2% and signaled rate hikes are needed, adding pressure to JPY-sensitive trades. Conversely, PBoC hinted at a potential rate cut this year amid Chinese growth weakness. ECB comments remain consistent with further tightening, with another (final) hike expected in September. Fed's Warsh signaled confidence; inflation expected to ease as Iran conflict subsides. Central bank divergence is a key cross-asset driver into H2.
